correctness.rationale: Any three columns (1,t,t^2) are independent over F, so a nontrivial signed triple-multiplicity relation uses all four sites. Cancelling a common site would give a two-sum equality, whose first and second moments determine both roots of the corresponding quadratic in odd characteristic. Thus only signs and permutations of (3,-1,-1,-1) and (2,1,-2,-1) remain. The one-dimensional kernel cannot contain two different relations up to sign: the repeated-entry pattern distinguishes the types; the triple repetition fixes the distinguished site in the first type; a scalar preserving {1,-1,2,-2} must be +/-1, since 4 is not in the set at characteristic >=7. In the first case translation makes the three arms the nonzero roots of X^3 minus their product, forcing the cube-root orbit and a unique center, so there are q(q-1)/3 sets when they exist. In the second, translating one doubled site to zero gives the offsets {0,x,-x/2,3x/2}, an affine copy of {0,1,3,4}; uniqueness of the signed relation restricts the stabilizer to the identity and reversal, both realized. This gives q(q-1)/2 and the generic count by subtraction, including extension fields. Fourier expansion with the q^4 factor leaves exactly the squared triple-convolution coefficients: diagonal weights are 1, 9 and 36 and give H=s^3+6se_2+12e_3; the isolated collision adds the stated real cross term. Equal squared magnitudes maximize both symmetric polynomials at fixed s in the generic case. In the unbalanced case, fixing center mass and positive arm mass, the outer e_2 and product are maximized together only by equal arms, and phase alignment attains the upper bound. Center-only has quotient 1, below the equal-four test. For positive arm mass the remaining quotient is Phi(r); differentiation gives -36r times the stated quartic divided by (r^2+3)^4. Descartes' rule and signs at zero and infinity give a unique positive root, the interior global maximum. All moduli are nonzero there and equality forces precisely the claimed phase condition. The exact boxed value is correct; the displayed decimal has a last-place rounding error, not a different theorem. For replay, evaluate the quartic in exact rational arithmetic at l=1.11264698453218643192147409131669 and h=1.11264698453218643192147409131670, obtaining opposite signs. With N and D the positive-coefficient numerator and denominator of Phi, bound it between N(l)/D(h) and N(h)/D(l), which lie strictly between 4.20323339946841509360 and 4.20323339946841509361. Thus the decimal prefix should be 4.203233399468415..., not ...414. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; finite tests are not needed for the field-uniform proof.
